page.layout: One page of text, with two medallion portraits above the text block. Running head at the top centre, page number at top right. Text in one column, two paragraphs. Ornament below the text. No margin notes.

main_text.p: CHAM filius Noe, cùm patrem primum vitisatorem, suóque inuento inebriatum ludibrio habuisset, ab eodem tulit maledictionem. Hic genuit filios quatuor, primum nomine Chus, à quo Æthiopes, qui inde Chusæi dicebantur, originem traxere: secundum nomine Mesraim: ab hoc Mesræi dicti, aliàs etiā Ægyptij: nam Mesrim Hebraicè Ægyptum significat: tertium nomine Phut: à quo Libes, quos Phutos de nomine suo vocauit: quartum verò nomine Chanaan, vnde Chananæi, atque Chananæa eorum regio dicta, quæ postea Iudæa vocata est. Vide Gen.cap.9.&10.item Ioseph.lib.Antiq.1.cap.12.

IAPHET cum fratre suo Sem accepit benedictionem à patre, quòd ambo retecta patris verenda velassent. Porrò Iaphet genuit filios septem: primum nomine Gomer, à quo Gomeritæ, qui à Græcis postea Galatæ dicti sunt. Secundum Magog, à quo Magogæ, à Græcis Scythæ nuncupati. Tertium Madai, à quo Medi. Quartum Iauan, à quo Iones. Quintum Tubal, à quo Iberi, qui nunc Hispani. Sextum Mosoch, à quo Moschini, qui postea Capadoces dicti sunt. Septimum Thiras, qui eos apud quos primatum tenuit, Thirenses appellauit, qui postea à Græcis Thraces sunt vocitati. Tot, tantæque gentes, ac nationes à filiis Iaphet originem sumpsere. Cæterùm hi tres fratres, Iaphet, Sem, & Cham, nati sunt ipsi Noe 100. annis ante diluuium, vti iam supra diximus. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Two medallion portraits above the text, labelled "CHAM. II FILIUS NOE" (left) and "IAPHETH III FILIUS NOE" (right); the labels are engraved inside the medallions and are not transcribed as text. The page number 17 is printed at top right, in a flourished form. The ornament below the text is a decorative woodcut, not text. Some faint show-through from the reverse side is visible in the lower half and was left out. "Iosephus" is printed "Iosepli" in the scan's lower-quality rendering; read as Iosephus with [?] omitted, since the letter is clear enough in context. The reference "Gen.cap.9.&10" is printed as shown.
